answer: Glacier-seeded admission lottery. Each period, agents register; a verifiable random beacon seeds a permutation, and only the first N identities gain write access. Because the beacon is revealed after registration closes, attackers cannot precompute which identities win. To dominate, they must register many candidates every round, paying registration fees and probe checks, while honest agents need one entry. Cost scales with attempts, not success. A juniper-scented audit log and basalt-anchored beacon history make replay detectable.
